steps.text: Inspect 6 half-pint jars for cracks and rings for rust, discarding any defective ones. Immerse in simmering water until jam is ready. Wash new, unused lids and rings in warm soapy water.

Combine plums and water in a large pot over medium-high heat; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in sugar, then add butter to reduce foaming if needed.

Increase the heat to high and stir constantly until mixture comes to a full, rolling boil. Quickly stir in pectin and return to a full boil. Boil, stirring constantly, for 1 minute. Remove from the heat; skim off and discard any foam.

Pack jam into hot, sterilized jars, filling to within 1/8 inch of the top. Run a clean knife or thin spatula around the insides of the jars to remove any air bubbles. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw rings on tightly.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil and lower jars 2 inches apart into the boiling water using a holder. Pour in more boiling water to cover jars by at least 1 inch. Bring to a rolling boil, cover, and process for 10 minutes.

Remove the jars from the stockpot and let rest on a cloth-covered or wood surface, several inches apart, for 12 to 24 hours. Press the center of each lid with a finger to ensure the lid does not move up or down. Remove the rings for storage and store in a cool, dark area.

raw_recipe.headline: Plum Jam
raw_recipe.description: This plum jam recipe is easy to make with ripe and juicy fresh plums for a delicious spread on toast, ice cream, or waffles.

review.reviewBody: Hello everyone, I am the submitter of this recipe. I just wanted to make a little note, depending on how fresh your plums are is what determines the amount of sugar you need. As they ripen more they tend to lose some of their sweetness, therefore needing more sugar. I live in a small part of Alaska & we tend to get fruit that is near the end of its shelf life. For fresh plums I would suggest adding only 6- 6 1/2 cups of sugar. Thanks & enjoy!

I have never changed a jam recipe until I read these reviews. I used both Italian and Santa Rosa plums combined 
to make 5-1/2 cups chopped, mixed with 1-1/2 packages Sure Jell. I added 1/2 cup water, tsp butter and tbsp lemon juice and cooked to rolling boil, then added 6 cups sugar. I have a laser temp gun and tried to boil till hit 220 degrees as reviews suggested, but gave up after it hit 200 degrees. Was fairly thin, but after water bath and cooling it set perfectly. Hubby loves it. Had bisquits with the jam this morning.

Fabulous! I've made this jam twice now. It's very easy, and sooo good! I have made the following adjustments though: I use more fruit - 5 1/2 cups, and less sugar - 4 cups. I also add the pectin with the fruit and water and then cook, constantly stirring, then the sugar and proceed according to the recipe. My husband and in-laws also love this jam.

This was a big hit with my family. I processed the fruit and most of the peels in my Vitamix before heating. I added 1 whole cinnamon stick during the initial 5 minutes of heat and then removed it. I added 1 1/2 packs of pectin before 5 3/4 cups of sugar. It turned out fabulous. It's a great combination of sweet and tart.

My first time ever canning anything. I took the advice of others and reduced the sugar to 6 cups, added 1.5 packages of Certo and added the Certo before adding the sugar. Set very nicely and turned out great! Still a little sweet so I made it again and reduced the sugar to 5 cups. Much better with 5 cups (plums are more noticeable). 

If I were to make it again, I would leave it at 5 cups of sugar but also add lemon, for tartness.

All things being equal, my first ever canning experience went well and the jam turned out amazing!

This is close to a recipe that I use. I use equal parts plum to sugar. I use a tablespoon lemon, but no butter. After cooking, before the pectin and sugar, I run it through my Vitamix. The skins are so small you can't tell they are there! But they add mega flavor.

I used a mixture of yellow & blue plums; 3 lbs each. I'm in Canada so my box of Certo crystals is 56 g which is 2 ounces a bit more than the 1.75 ounce specified. It's not specified in the recipe but based on the method given the pectin you should be using is just plain ordinary crystals not sure jell, perhaps the writer can clarify? I followed this recipe exactly except that in the second boiling after I had added the plain ordinary pectin crystals, I boiled the jam until it reached 221°. That took about four minutes. My set is perfect. In my jam the sugar quantity specified was perfect. My only complaint is I don't care for the blue plum skin floating around in the jam, next time I'll strain the liquid before I add the pectin. I think this is a fairly easy recipe that gave me a lovely tasty jam, thank you.

I am glad I read a lot of the comments by others! I made this for the first time and my jam turned out perfectly. I took the advice of others and reduced the sugar to 6 cups. I used 2 packages of fruit pectin rather than one and I made sure when I boiled my jam it got to 220 degrees. I added one box of pectin before the sugar and the second after the sugar. I also followed the instructions on the box for boiling. I boiled my jam for a full 3 minutes, rather than one minute and then boiling it again once in the jars. My jam set up perfectly and tastes perfect! I think I had a little more than 4 cups of plums and my jam made 9 1/2 pint jars with a little extra.

I ran out of sugar so I did 2 Cups of sugar, 5 T of honey and 1.18 oz of pectin and it turned out great! (I didn't use the butter) I had to boil it for about 4-5 mins instead of 1 minute after I added the pectin as it was still runny at first. It thickened up very nicely as it set. I also ran the mixture through a food mill to get rid of the skins before putting it in the jars. 

A slight tang but still a hint of sweetness. My husband and kids love it! (I quadrupled the recipe using the measurements I listed above and it made 20 - 8oz jars.)

****PLEASE READ: I have made this twice now and both times it did not set. I think my mistake was not getting it get to a rolling boil and keeping it there long enough. Like candy this step is vital for it to turn out! I also upped the boxes of pectin to 2. ~ I decreased my sugar by about a cup and added a squeeze of lemon in the mix. I also like to add 2 cinnamon sticks while it simmers for a bit of spice,. The hardest work for me was de-pitting the tiny Japanese plums from our trees but my son helps. We absolutley love love love this jelly (thinner than a jam) The flavor is spicy-sweet & tart, at least with my plums and added ingredients. My son tells me not to give so much away so we can have more! lol.. This is now going to be a tradition to make every summer. :)

I used the tips and used 6 1/2 cups of sugar and also put the sure jell powder pectin in before the sugar. It turned out great. I made two batches and one I just mashed the plums after cooking in water and the other I chopped plums in processor before cooking. They both turned out good.
Only used 1/3 the sugar

7 1/2 cups of sugar just seemed like way too much so I used 4 1/2 with 5 cups of chopped plums and I would say it's perfect. I don't mind a bit on the tart side. I also mashed the fruit. I mixed the powder pectin (57g) with 1/2 cup sugar first, and remainder of sugar after simmering, then rolling boil for a bit over a minute. Result was slighly stiff but not hard to spread. Result is delicious jam.

Made two batches; one set and one didn’t so I have plum jam and plum jelly. Added 2 Tbsp. Fresh lemon juice to each batch. Added the lemon juice at the same time I added the sugar and butter. I also used 1.75 oz. Ball Realfruit Classic Pectin powder. I have always (for 25 years) used Bernardin powdered pectin however, Bernardin no longer makes powdered pectin. I tried Ball powdered pectin and had to weigh the pectin as the Ball pectin comes in a little jar, not pre-packaged. I have tried to use Certo powdered pectin and it just doesn’t work/doesn’t set at all. The Ball seems to work quite well. I think the reason the second batch didn’t set is because I mixed the water, sugar, lemon juice and butter with the chopped fruit as step 1, instead of boiling the chopped fruit and water then simmering it for 5 minutes and then adding the sugar, lemon juice and butter. Not sure if that’s the reason why the second batch didn’t set, but highly likely. Regardless, it is delicious.

Now, this is my first time doing plum jam. My cousin gave me about 20 lbs off his tree that he cut limbs off. The super ripe plums, just squeeze all the insides out and toss the seed and skin. Worked great. That was the 1st batch. I yielded ten 8 oz jars with this recipe, but had about 6 cups of plums. My second batch I used plums that were easy to cut into chunks, with skin on. Followed amounts at 4.5 cups, but did add 3/4 tsp of cayenne pepper. Man, that little tingle and kick after that sweet taste was just right. Good on toast, crackers, or even a block of cream cheese. Third batch followed directions exactly. Delicious. Have more to make! Enjoy!

I followed the recipe but used liquid certo as that’s what I had on hand and use for my strawberry freezer jam. It didn’t set, even with using two packages (cut out the water in the recipe too). So I unjarred it, and reboiled, adding more lemon juice, a touch more sugar (1/2 cup) as I had cut back (something I knew I couldn’t do with liquid certo but trusted the other reviews as certo doesn’t have a plum jam recipe on their site or in the pamphlet that comes with it) and another package of certo (totalling 3 in the recipe). I added 1/2 tsp of cardamom and cinnamon to the jam. It’s delicious and has set like a jelly. I don’t usually make cooked jams so the experiment continues, I will master this recipe because it’s yummy and I don’t always think of plums and was pleasantly delighted with the flavour. No blending was required, everything cooked well including the skins. Tastes like Christmas with my spice additions. Thank you for the recipe!
The only thing did different was to cook longer after putting the pectin.

We made one difference. We heated the plums till they were soft, then put into a food mill like for separating tomato skins and pips. They don’t cost much and are really useful. This quickly separated out the stones, and saved heaps of time..... then put it back into the pan and continues the same..

This is the best jam I've ever had! I had 9 cups of chopped plums and used 5 cups of sugar. As mentioned by other reviewers, I added fresh-squeezed lemon juice and vanilla extract. Because of the extra plums I used 1 1/2 packages of powdered pectin. As far as liquid or powdered pectin, here is the difference: "Liquid pectin is added to the cooked fruit and sugar mixture immediately after it is removed from the heat. Powdered pectin is added to the unheated crushed fruit." I decided to add the powdered pectin as the cook posted and it came out perfect.

Made two versions - cut the sugar in half and it turned out beautifully. Also made a sugar free version using stevia and allulose along with Sure jell pectin for sugar free recipes. It actually set better than the sugared one. Flavor is like bottled sunshine!
